Intended use: Compare algorithms on a declared benchmark
Evidence needed and inference supported: Evaluation against the same stated target, members and metric, with selection separated from evaluation, supports a within-benchmark comparison
What that evidence does not establish: Performance on a different negative population, source or intended use; evidence accumulation from newly collected samples
References: Walsh et al., 2021; Kapoor et al., 2024; Cawley and Talbot, 2010

Evidence needed and inference supported: Assays establish activity of the tested candidates. A measured ordering tests ranking within the sampled candidates; enrichment requires a relevant comparison sample
What that evidence does not establish: False-negative rates among untested candidates; superiority to another selection strategy without a corresponding comparison
References: Guan et al., 2023; Cheng et al., 2025; Walsh et al., 2021

Intended use: Predict numerical potency under defined conditions
Evidence needed and inference supported: Compare predicted values with independently measured concentration–response estimates under matched conditions, and assess numerical error; ranking agreement alone supports ordering
What that evidence does not establish: Quantitative accuracy from rank agreement alone, or transfer of numerical values across assays, materials or endpoints
References: Nongonierma and FitzGerald, 2016; Zan et al., 2023

Intended use: Claim an added effect in a processed food
Evidence needed and inference supported: Compare the specified food endpoint with a matched processed matrix or formulation control; this supports the measured incremental effect under those conditions
What that evidence does not establish: Attribution to one peptide without additional evidence, other endpoints, or human glycaemic benefit from an in vitro comparison alone
References: Yao et al., 2026; Tenenbaum et al., 2023
